study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting task-based fMRI activity using normative modelling: an application to the Emotional Face Matching Task

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Large-scale normative models of task-evoked fMRI activation (EFMT) are built to bind heterogeneous datasets to a common reference, quantify individual deviations, and relate them to transdiagnostic symptom domains; then applied to a naturalistic clinical cohort.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: UK Biobank; HCP Young Adult; HCP Development; AOMIC PIOP2; Duke Neurogenetics Study (DNS); MIND-Set (controls)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: Methods explicitly list six sites used to collate the reference sample for modelling the EFMT (with MIND-Set also containing a clinical population).
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Wecollated a large reference sample from 6 independent sites ... AOMIC PIOP2, Duke Neurogenetics Study, HCP Development, HCP Young Adult (1200 release), UK Biobank, and the MIND-Set cohort ...

rci2_hc_n.reason: The reference normative models were estimated using data from 7,728 individuals across the lifespan (post-QC, used for modelling).
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Next, we estimated normative models ... using data from 7728 individuals across the lifespan.

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: The study models task-evoked BOLD activation during the Emotional Face Matching Task (EFMT).
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Task-based functional neuroimaging (functional magnetic resonance imaging; fMRI) ... Emotional Face Matching Task (EFMT)

caa2_diseases_studied.answer: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD); Mood disorders; Anxiety disorders; Neurodivergence (co-occurring possible)
caa2_diseases_studied.reason: Main text lists ASD, ADHD, and mood/anxiety disorders; acknowledges co-occurrence and heterogeneity.
caa2_diseases_studied.supporting_text: ... patients with a current diagnosis (mood and anxiety disorders, ASD and/or ADHD) ... co-occurring and heterogeneous ...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Patients show a higher frequency of extreme deviations for faces>shapes with heterogeneous spatial distribution; faces>baseline models relate more strongly to transdiagnostic functioning; normative deviations predict functional domains via SCCA, while diagnosis labels show little association.
